title: Finite filtered comparison from bounded-below second-page comparison
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] admitting derived categories and K-injective right-derived functors [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For a small set I let $K_i,S\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $u_i:K_i\to S$ have a common cohomological lower bound a. Fix q in Z. Assume for every p >= 0 and r in Z that the canonical map $\bigoplus_i H^p(RF(H^r(K_i)[0]))\to H^p(RF(H^r(S)[0]))$ induced by H^r(u_i) is an isomorphism. Then there exist finite decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration] FS on $\bigoplus_i H^q(RF(K_i))$ and FT on $H^q(RF(S))$ and a filtered morphism phi whose underlying map is the canonical sum of H^q(RF(u_i)), such that every graded map [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] of phi is an isomorphism. No coproduct hypothesis on the u_i in the derived category is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the natural source coproduct and target truncation couples and their morphism from lem-pc-coproduct-truncation-couple. At negative first indices both E terms are zero. At nonnegative first indices the natural E comparison equation and hE2 make T_E an isomorphism, since it is conjugate to the canonical second-page comparison by the supplied isomorphisms.

Prove directly that T_D is invertible at every bidegree. It is invertible below the common lower bound, as a morphism between zero objects. Induct on the nonnegative distance of the second index from a-1. The exact-couple axioms give the exact row E^{p-1,r} -> D^{p+1,r-1} -> D^{p,r} -> E^{p,r} -> D^{p+2,r-1}. T gives a commuting five-term diagram. Both E components are invertible by the preceding step and the two D components of second index r-1 are invertible by induction. Mathlib Abelian.isIso_of_epi_of_isIso_of_isIso_of_mono gives invertibility of the middle component. Transport arithmetic indices explicitly in the Lean proof. The supplied canonical D comparison equation conjugates T_D^{0,q} into the required Sigma.desc, which is therefore an isomorphism.

For any object take the one-step filtration, full for p<=0 and zero for p>0, finite with bounds 0 and 1. Any morphism has a filtered lift between these two matching filtrations: at a full step use the invertible top inclusions, and at a zero step use the zero map. For an underlying isomorphism, every restriction is an isomorphism: cancel the invertible top inclusion in the full case, and use that both bottom-step objects are zero in the other case. The defining equation of exists_gradedMap and the cokernel universal property identify gradedMap with cokernel.map of the two successive restrictions. Mathlib cokernel.map is invertible when these restrictions are invertible. Use these actual, matching one-step filtrations for the canonical abutment isomorphism and introduce all requested witnesses. This works also for q<a and for an empty family.

proof_origin.place: Natural truncation construction followed by direct five-lemma induction and a proved one-step filtration construction, R1

mathlib_searches.query: spectral sequence coproduct comparison bounded below hypercohomology finite filtration graded isomorphisms
A morphism from a coproduct of bounded below derived objects has finite hypercohomology filtrations with isomorphic graded maps if the second page comparison is an isomorphism

lean.statement:
theorem exists_boundedBelow_coproduct_filtration
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{v} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} B]
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    (I : Type v) (K : I → DerivedCategory A) (S : DerivedCategory A)
    (u : ∀ i, K i ⟶ S) (a q : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ (i : I) (r : ℤ), r < a →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj (K i)))
    (hS : ∀ r : ℤ, r < a → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).obj S))
    (hE2 : ∀ (p : ℕ) (r : ℤ), IsIso (Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0 ⋙ F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B (p : ℤ)).map
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A r).map (u i))))) :
    ∃ (FS : DecreasingFiltration
        (∐ (fun i ↦ (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B q).obj
          (K i))))
      (FT : DecreasingFiltration
        ((F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B q).obj S))
      (phi : FilteredObject.Hom ⟨_, FS⟩ ⟨_, FT⟩),
      FS.IsFinite ∧ FT.IsFinite ∧
        phi.hom = Sigma.desc (fun i ↦
          (F.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor B q).map (u i)) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, IsIso (FilteredObject.gradedMap phi p)
